Q: Firebase Authentication: EMAIL_TEMPLATE_UPDATE_NOT_ALLOWED when updating custom action URL (Identity Platform project) A:

Firebase seems to recently have started blocking such updates to email templates. From a Reddit thread about this where the Firebase support team answered:

due to a temporary business decision template updates are restricted to prevent abuse.

The support team gave two options there:

  • They can escalate to the engineering team on your behalf, who can then make the change for you.

  • You can replace the standard Firebase client-side password reset process by a backend-mediated flow.

    This allows the application to still use the Firebase Authentication but sending totally customised email templates using custom action handler and external email service.

    You can use the Firebase Admin SDK to generate the secure action link, embed it into your custom HTML email template, and send it using your own SMTP server. This gives you complete control over both the design and the delivery process.

If you want to follow the second process, there should be some relevant content both here and in blog posts that cover it. If you want to follow the first process, open a case with the support team.

Q: Excel formula to determine if any cells in a range contain a value A:

Maybe this is overkill, but here is how I would solve it.

Premise

You have two things you wish to check for:

  • Either at least one cell is true.

  • Or all the cells are false.

Here is the structure you proposed:

A
1 formula
2 text
3 boolean
4 boolean
5 boolean

We need two formulas to work it out:

  • =COUNTIF(A3:A5; TRUE)>0: This returns the number of true results.
  • =ROWS(A3:A5)=COUNTIF(A3:A3;FALSE): This returns true if all cells are false.

Solutions

It appears I have misread your desired output, so I here provide two solutions. I added line breaks and indentation to ease the reading. Replace semicolons with commas depending on your language settings.

Solution one

This returns TRUE if at least one cell is TRUE, FALSE if all cells are FALSE, and an error message otherwise.

=IF(
    COUNTIF(A3:A5;TRUE)>0;
    TRUE;
    IF(
       ROWS(A3:A5)=COUNTIF(A3:A5;FALSE);
       FALSE;
       "Error in input")

Solution two

As pointed out in the comment, this is probably a misreading of what you (O.P.) actually wanted. This formula therefore does the following:

If either there is at least one true statement or the number of cells that are false equal the number of rows (i.e. all cells are false), then return TRUE; otherwise return FALSE. The two latter parts can be changed to numbers, text prompts, or whatever suits your needs.

=IF(
    OR(COUNTIF(A3:A5;TRUE)>0;
       ROWS(A3:A5)=COUNTIF(A3:A5;FALSE));
    TRUE;
    FALSE)

Q: What's the simplest way to list conflicted files in Git? A: 
git status --short | grep '^(.U|U.|AA|DD) '

The grep expression above matches all the conflicted states in the docs for --short output and none of the other states. Regex golfed by Michael in 2019 in the comments below.
